title: SDK client entrance rubric: enterprise auth adapters + resumable streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Over the last 8 weeks we collected 28 distinct enterprise asks about client libraries: primary themes are (1) language bindings (Go, Swift, Rust) with production idioms, (2) pluggable auth patterns (token rotation, customer KMS, mTLS, SSO SAML/OIDC), and (3) resumable/partial-response streaming semantics for unreliable mobile networks. Goal: produce a reproducible intake and prioritization rubric that outputs a ranked backlog plus a small MVP scope for Q2 to unblock 3 pilot customers. This ticket captures the rubric draft, proposal of MVP deliverables, and next steps for engineering/design alignment.
acceptance_criteria: A triage rubric exists that scores requests across: customer scale, security constraints, engineering effort, operator burden, and latency impact

MVP scope defined: language adapters for Go + Swift, an auth adapter pattern doc (token-rotation + KMS integration pattern), and a streaming SDK example supporting resumable streams with clear backpressure semantics
Stakeholders (Eng/runtime, Design, Security, Solutions) have reviewed and approved the rubric and MVP scope
Roadmap entry created and linked to Dedicated/Private onboarding checklist
Telemetry plan defined for post-release signal collection (error rates, reconnection rate, average resume time)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full multi-language parity vs. canonical reference implementation + forks. Recommendation: build canonical reference in TypeScript and Go; provide pattern docs for other languages to reduce triage cost.

Engineering asks: need 3 weeks of runtime effort for streaming adaptors, and a separate 2-week spike for secure token rotation flow with KMS; propose to sequence token flow first to unblock compliance reviews.
Design guideline: streaming ergonomics should favor explicit resume tokens + short-lived ephemeral sessionless tokens; avoid hidden reconnection logic that obscures audit trails.
